_about: Representation-only rows for tools/fidelity/struct_compare.py: where the old engine's game view and the game's record differ in how a state is written, not in the state. Each row: id, kind (struct_compare.KINDS says what each does), its parameters, why it is representation only, and the legacy comparer's rule it stands for. Patterns are globs over schema paths (indices written [*], keyed entries {*}): * matches within one path segment, ** across segments. 'when' restricts a row to steps whose record says so. docs/rebuild/COMPARER.md explains the kinds. engines lists the engines a row applies to: old for rows that exist only because of the old engine's limits, * for every engine.

rows.reason: The game's snapshot can list an enemy at 0 HP while it dies; a dead enemy is no state either side plays on, and the engine writes the living roster.

A lost fight ends the run: the game stops the combat at the killing hit, the old engine plays the enemy phase out, and nothing that is left is carried on. Only in_combat and the player's HP are compared.

The old engine holds every subclass of the game's TemporaryStrengthPower (TemporaryDexterityPower, TemporaryFocusPower) in one buff, and SelfFormingClayPower in BlockNextTurnPower's, with the summed amount; it cannot say which subclass. Both sides' members are summed into the base power before comparing.

The old engine has five intent kinds and at most two intents a move; the game has more kinds (DebuffStrong, StatusCard, Summon...) and moves of three intents. An intents diff is allowed when the first intent's class and the first damage intent's [damage, hits] agree; a kind outside the map (Summon, Escape...) keeps its own name, so two different unmapped kinds differ; the old engine writes Unknown for what its five kinds cannot say, and that stands for any unmapped kind of the record.
The old engine's moves are positions in its own AI tables; it has no game move id. The move's intents are compared (intent-vocabulary).
rows.legacy: fight_compare.game_view: the move id is not compared, only game_intent of the move's intents

rows.reason: Seeds are fixed by the run's seed; the old engine writes the streams' counters, which are compared.
rows.legacy: fight_compare: rng counter only; netstate_diff: not modelled (rng.seed game only)

rows.reason: The game's network sequencing counters and turn phase; the old engine has no phases between steps.
rows.legacy: netstate_diff: not modelled (game-only paths are not compared)

rows.reason: [SavedProperty] values and FloorAddedToDeck have no field in the old engine (its relic counter has no common unit with the game's named props and is in its private block).
rows.legacy: netstate_diff.flat: relics.props/relics.floor and piles.*.props/floor written for the game side only

rows.reason: The old engine prices the hand only (EffectiveCost prices a card about to be played; some game cost hooks look at the pile).
The old engine models Bound as a flag, so its affliction has no amount; the affliction's id is compared.
The old engine holds upgraded as a flag; the game counts upgrades. Upgraded on both sides is the same card to the old engine.
The old engine's relic counter is its own unit (private block); the game's snapshot has none yet.
rows.legacy: fight_compare.OPTIONAL: .relic_counters compared only where both sides wrote it

rows.reason: Once a fight is over the run holds no energy and no round; the game's snapshot still writes the last ones.
rows.legacy: fight_compare._game_end_view: no energy (and round is never compared)

rows.reason: The game's last checkpoint of a step can precede work the game did after it (the auto-play after 'After player turn start'); where the record's own snapshot moved past its last checkpoint, the net path is judged by the snapshot comparison of the same step.
Record integrity, not the engine: a step whose action left no checksum was recorded before the game finished it; the net shape is not compared from the suspect step on (the snapshot still is).

With a kernel switch on, core2 writes the game's lastExecutedActionId and lastExecutedHookId from its own action queue's counters. The record's ids come from the live game's synchronizer, which also numbers actions the emulator does not run, so the two are not the same count: the paths are listed as surplus of the census and not compared. Where core2 writes none (no switch on) the record's side stays under net-sequencing.
rows.legacy: none: netstate_diff does not model the sequencing ids
